name: Franz Josef and Fox Glacier
tagline: A rare pairing of glaciers descending almost to temperate rainforest, reached by a wild, sparsely populated stretch of the West Coast.
highlight: Standing on Franz Josef's ice by helicopter, the glacier's crevassed surface spread out beneath you and dense rainforest visible in the valley below.
shortDescription: Twin glaciers on New Zealand's West Coast, their ice descending unusually close to rainforest and coastline for a rare landscape combination.
metaDescription: A Franz Josef and Fox Glacier travel guide: heli-hikes, Lake Matheson, the valley walks, when to go and how to plan your visit.
knownFor: Glacier heli-hikes, Lake Matheson's reflections, rainforest-to-ice scenery
goodFor: Glacier scenery, heli-hikes, a quieter stretch of the South Island

image.alt: Franz Josef Glacier descending from the Southern Alps

intro: Franz Josef and Fox, twin glaciers a short drive apart on the South Island's West Coast, are unusual worldwide for how far they descend toward sea level and temperate rainforest — a combination of steep terrain and heavy Tasman Sea rainfall found in only a handful of places on Earth.

Both sit within Te Wahipounamu, the same UNESCO World Heritage area that covers Fiordland, and both are retreating overall even as they occasionally advance in wetter years, a visible, ongoing reminder of the wider glacier's response to a changing climate.

The two small townships that share the glaciers' names are quiet, practical bases rather than resort towns — most visitors are here for a specific activity, whether a valley walk, a scenic flight or a heli-hike onto the ice itself.

whyVisit.intro: Franz Josef and Fox's case rests on a rare landscape combination found in very few places worldwide.

points.title: The glaciers descend close to rainforest, a rare combination anywhere on Earth
points.text: Steep terrain and heavy coastal rainfall bring the ice unusually close to temperate forest and the sea.

points.title: Lake Matheson's reflections are among the most photographed in New Zealand
points.text: On a still morning, Aoraki/Mount Cook and Mount Tasman reflect perfectly in the lake's dark water.

points.title: The heli-hike is a rare chance to walk on the ice itself
points.text: Retreat has made the glacier face largely unsafe to approach on foot, so helicopters now land hikers directly on the upper ice.

points.title: The West Coast setting is quieter than the rest of the South Island's big-name stops
points.text: Sparse population and dramatic, wild scenery give it a different character from Queenstown or Milford Sound.

points.title: It's an easy, natural link on a South Island road trip
points.text: The main highway connects it directly to Queenstown in the south and Abel Tasman and Nelson to the north.

attractionsIntro: Franz Josef and Fox's essential sights span both glaciers, a famous mirror lake, and the rainforest and wetlands around them.

attractions.name: Franz Josef Glacier

image.alt: Franz Josef Glacier descending from the Southern Alps

attractions.text: The more visited of the two glaciers, its ice descending a steep valley almost to the surrounding rainforest.
attractions.tip: The glacier face itself is off-limits to walkers now — a heli-hike or scenic flight is the way to get close.

attractions.name: Fox Glacier

image.file: File:Fox Glacier in Westland National Park 06.jpg
image.alt: Fox Glacier flowing through Westland National Park

attractions.text: A quieter, slightly larger neighbour to Franz Josef, a short drive south, with its own valley walk and viewpoints.
attractions.tip: Visiting both glaciers works well as a single day if you're based between the two townships.

attractions.name: Lake Matheson

image.file: File:Lake Matheson reflection of Mount Tasman and Aoraki Mount Cook.jpg
image.alt: Lake Matheson's mirror reflection of Aoraki/Mount Cook and Mount Tasman

attractions.text: A famous mirror lake near Fox Glacier, its still water reflecting Aoraki/Mount Cook and Mount Tasman on calm mornings.
attractions.tip: Arrive at dawn — wind picks up later and breaks the reflection within a few hours.

attractions.name: The glacier heli-hike

image.alt: A helicopter landed on the ice for a glacier heli-hike

attractions.text: A rare chance to walk directly on glacier ice, landing above the crevassed lower sections that are no longer safely accessible on foot.
attractions.tip: Book with real flexibility — heli-hikes are weather-dependent and cancel or delay often.

attractions.name: Okarito Lagoon

image.alt: Okarito Lagoon, New Zealand's largest unmodified wetland

attractions.text: New Zealand's largest unmodified wetland, a short drive from Franz Josef, home to kiwi and a wealth of coastal birdlife.
attractions.tip: A guided kayak trip at dawn or dusk is the best way to spot the resident white heron colony.

attractions.name: The West Coast rainforest

image.file: File:West Coast Treetop Walk, rimu rainforest - WestCoastTreetop8773.jpg
image.alt: An elevated walkway through West Coast rainforest

attractions.text: A lush temperate rainforest surrounds both glacier valleys, an elevated treetop walkway near Hokitika showing it from above.
attractions.tip: It's a worthwhile stop on the drive between the glaciers and Hokitika.

attractions.name: The glacier valley walk

image.alt: Walking the valley track toward Franz Josef Glacier

attractions.text: An easy walk up the valley floor toward the glacier terminal, showing the dramatic scale of the ice's historic retreat.
attractions.tip: Markers along the track show past ice extent by year — a sobering, visible record of retreat.

thingsToDoIntro: Franz Josef and Fox reward getting close to the ice, on foot, by air or from the surrounding wetlands and forest.

thingsToDo.title: Heli-hike onto the glacier

image.alt: A helicopter preparing for a glacier heli-hike landing

thingsToDo.text: The essential Franz Josef and Fox experience, landing above the crevassed lower ice for a guided walk on the glacier itself.
thingsToDo.tip: Book on the first available day of your visit — leave a spare day in case of weather cancellation.

thingsToDo.title: Walk the glacier valley track

image.alt: Walking the valley track toward the glacier

thingsToDo.text: An easy, flat walk suited to any fitness level, following the valley floor as close to the ice as ground access now allows.
thingsToDo.tip: Check current track status before setting out — sections close after heavy rain or rockfall.

thingsToDo.title: See Lake Matheson's dawn reflections

image.file: File:Lake Matheson reflection of Mount Tasman and Aoraki Mount Cook.jpg

thingsToDo.text: An early start rewards you with the calmest water and the clearest mirror reflection of the peaks.
thingsToDo.tip: The full loop track takes about 1.5 hours — allow time beyond just the viewpoint.

thingsToDo.title: Kayak or spot birdlife at Okarito Lagoon
thingsToDo.text: A peaceful contrast to the glaciers, paddling New Zealand's largest unmodified wetland among herons and other coastal birds.
thingsToDo.tip: Guided dawn tours offer the best chance of a white heron sighting.

thingsToDo.title: Walk the West Coast Treetop Walk

image.file: File:West Coast Treetop Walk, rimu rainforest - WestCoastTreetop8773.jpg
image.alt: The elevated West Coast Treetop Walk through rainforest

thingsToDo.text: An elevated steel walkway lifts you into the rainforest canopy, a striking contrast to the ice just up the road.
thingsToDo.tip: A worthwhile detour on the drive north toward Hokitika.

thingsToDo.title: Soak in the Glacier Hot Pools
thingsToDo.text: A welcome way to end a cold day on the ice, natural-style hot pools set among rainforest right in Franz Josef township.
thingsToDo.tip: Evening sessions are popular in winter — book ahead if visiting then.

accommodation.intro: Franz Josef and Fox Glacier townships are small and a short drive apart, each a workable base for both glaciers.

areas.name: Franz Josef township
areas.bestFor: The widest choice of accommodation and heli-hike operators
areas.text: The larger and busier of the two townships, with the Glacier Hot Pools right in town.

areas.name: Fox Glacier township
areas.bestFor: A quieter stay, close to Lake Matheson
areas.text: Smaller and more relaxed, with easy access to the mirror lake.

gettingThere.intro: Franz Josef and Fox sit remotely on the West Coast, reached by a long but spectacular drive from either direction.

options.text: About 4-4.5 hours' drive via Haast Pass, one of the South Island's great road-trip routes.
options.detail: Fuel up before Haast — services are sparse along this stretch.

options.text: About 5.5 hours via Arthur's Pass, another dramatic mountain crossing.
options.detail: A natural link if arriving from [[christchurch|Christchurch]] rather than the south.

options.text: Small regional flights connect Hokitika, about an hour north, to Christchurch.
options.detail: A useful option to skip part of the long drive.

gettingAround.intro: Both glacier townships are tiny and walkable, with a car or organised transfer needed to reach the ice and Lake Matheson.

options.text: Both townships are small enough to cover on foot, including reaching the start of the valley walks.
options.detail: Lake Matheson and the glacier heli-hike bases are a short drive from Fox and Franz Josef townships respectively.

options.text: The most flexible way to move between the two glaciers and Lake Matheson.
options.detail: The drive between the two townships takes about 25 minutes.

options.text: Essential for reaching the glacier ice itself, and widely available from both townships.
options.detail: Operators typically include transfers from your accommodation.

bestTime.headline: Any season, though heli-hikes are more weather-dependent in winter
bestTime.summary: The glaciers themselves are visible year-round, though flying conditions and daylight hours shift the experience by season.

seasons.text: The most reliable flying conditions and longest daylight hours for heli-hikes and walks.
Settled and quieter than summer, with good flying conditions still common.
Dramatic snow-covered scenery, though heli-hikes cancel more often due to weather.
Increasingly settled, a good shoulder season before summer's crowds arrive.

bestTime.avoid: Nothing strongly — build a spare day into any visit regardless of season, since heli-hikes and scenic flights are weather-dependent throughout the year.

tipsIntro: Practical notes on weather, booking and driving that make a real difference to a Franz Josef and Fox trip.
tips: Build a spare day into your visit — heli-hikes cancel or delay often due to weather.
Book your heli-hike for the first available day, holding your buffer day in reserve.
Arrive at Lake Matheson at dawn — wind picks up within a few hours and breaks the reflection.
Fill your fuel tank before driving Haast Pass — services are sparse along the route.
Pack sandfly repellent — they're persistent around both townships and the lagoon.
Check current valley walk track status before setting out — sections close after heavy rain.

faq.q: Can you still walk right up to the glacier?
faq.a: Not all the way — retreat has made the lower ice face unstable, so ground access stops short and a heli-hike is the way to get onto the ice itself.

faq.q: Is the heli-hike worth the cost?
faq.a: Yes, for most visitors — it's a rare chance to walk on real glacier ice, and reviews consistently rate it among the best experiences in New Zealand.

faq.q: How many days do you need at Franz Josef and Fox?
faq.a: Two days covers both glaciers, Lake Matheson and a heli-hike, with a spare day advisable given how weather-dependent flying is.

faq.q: Which is better, Franz Josef or Fox Glacier?
faq.a: Similar in quality — Franz Josef has more infrastructure and operators, while Fox pairs naturally with Lake Matheson's reflections.

faq.q: Is the drive from Queenstown difficult?
faq.a: Long but manageable — about 4-4.5 hours via Haast Pass, with spectacular scenery throughout, though fuel stops are sparse.

faq.q: Do the glaciers ever advance instead of retreat?
faq.a: Occasionally, in unusually wet years, though the long-term trend for both glaciers has been retreat.
